sceneTurns.text: "Keep the little lantern burning until morning,"

Anna whispered. The old stone bridge stood above the river while the evening light faded slowly. Below the narrow arch the water carried fallen leaves towards the distant sea. A small brass bell hung beside the gate and moved gently in the cool wind.

The path beyond the garden curved between tall trees and disappeared behind a hill. Across the valley the empty station waited beneath a pale and cloudless autumn sky. Its wooden benches held a thin layer of dust from the road outside the fence.

Beside the closed ticket window a clock continued counting every quiet minute of the night. The railway tracks shone softly where the moonlight reached them through the branches overhead. Nothing moved on the platform except a loose paper turning slowly near the doorway.
At dawn the eastern clouds became pink and the fields emerged from the silver mist. The first light touched the roofs and windows of the houses along the winding road.
Smoke rose above the village as the baker opened the door beside the market square. Far beyond the last house the river continued quietly towards the open and waiting sea.
